issue: Under § 403(b) of the First Step Act, is a sentence that was later vacated on direct appeal because of a constitutional defect 'imposed' before the Act's enactment, so that the defendant is excluded from the Act's sentencing relief?
provision: First Step Act of 2018, Pub. L. No. 115-391, § 403(b), 132 Stat. 5194, 5222

sides.position: A vacated sentence is not 'imposed' for § 403(b) purposes because vacatur voids the sentence ab initio, so defendants whose pre-Act sentences were vacated for a constitutional defect may receive the Act's resentencing relief
cases: United States v. Uriarte, 975 F.3d 596 (7th Cir. 2020) (en banc)
United States v. Bethea, 841 F. App'x 544 (4th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Henry, 983 F.3d 214 (6th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Merrell, 2022 WL 2092588 (9th Cir. June 10, 2022)
United States v. Mitchell, 38 F.4th 382 (3d Cir. 2022)

sides.position: A sentence vacated on appeal is 'imposed' for § 403(b) purposes because vacatur only erases its legal effect going forward, so defendants whose pre-Act sentences were later vacated are not covered by the Act
cases: United States v. Jackson, 995 F.3d 522 (6th Cir. 2021)

this_court: The Third Circuit holds that a vacated sentence is not 'imposed,' so § 403(b) applies to the defendant's resentencing, joining the Uriarte side and rejecting Jackson.
quote: Our sister circuits have split on this question under the Act.
cite: United States v. Tyrone Mitchell, 38 F.4th 382 (3rd Cir. 2022)
